lesson.intro: Bentuk sejajar (parallel structure) berarti bagian-bagian yang setara dalam kalimat memakai bentuk kata yang sama. Pola ini membuat daftar terdengar rapi dan membantu pembaca memprediksi apa yang datang berikutnya.

sections.heading: Daftar dengan tiga item
sections.bodyMd: Dalam daftar, semua item harus memakai bentuk yang sama. **She likes reading, writing, and drawing.** Semua item berbentuk -ing. Kalimat **She likes reading, to write, and drawing** tidak sejajar, karena item kedua memakai infinitif.

sections.heading: Pasangan not only ___ but also dan both ___ and
sections.bodyMd: Setelah **not only** dan **but also**, bentuknya harus sama: **He not only sings but also dances.** Setelah **both ___ and**, kedua bagian juga harus sama: **Both the teachers and the students arrive early.**

sections.heading: Perbandingan
sections.bodyMd: Hal yang dibandingkan harus memakai bentuk yang sama: **The tasks in unit one are easy, and the tasks in unit two are hard.** Jangan membandingkan kata benda dengan kata kerja atau kata sifat.

block3.title: Mengapa Kesejajaran Penting
block3.text:
Good writers keep a good balance in their sentences. When a list contains several items, each item should have a similar form. This principle is called parallel structure. For example, the sentence She likes reading, writing, and drawing is consistent, because each activity ends in -ing. The sentence She likes reading, to write, and drawing breaks the pattern and sounds awkward.

Parallel structure also matters in comparisons. Two things that are compared should match in form. The sentence The tasks in the first unit are as easy as the tasks in the second unit is clear and equal in weight. A sentence that says The tasks in the first unit are easy, but the second unit is more difficult for the students is less balanced, because the two parts do not follow the same sequence of ideas.

Many learners think that parallel structure is only about grammar, but it also helps readers follow the main point. When a writer uses the same grammatical pattern for each idea, the reader can predict what comes next. This makes the text easier to read and gives the writing a sense of symmetry.

Parallel structure also appears in paired expressions. Words such as both, either, and neither are often followed by items that must match. For example, both the teacher and the students need to arrive early. The two parts of the pair must have the same grammatical form, so the sentence looks similar on both sides of the connector.

To check your work, read the sentence aloud and listen for an uneven rhythm. Then compare each item in the list. If one item is a noun and another is a verb, rewrite the list so that every item has the same form. A short check like this takes only a minute, but it can make a long essay much more professional.
